label: Confirmed Cases (2026 DRC + Uganda + France)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / WHO / UN News / Al Jazeera — 20–21 August 2026
contestNote: DRC: 5,290 confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths as of 19 August, published 20 August (81 new cases: Ituri 56, North Kivu 18, Haut-Uélé 7). Uganda's outbreak was declared officially over 28 July 2026 (20 confirmed, 18 recoveries, 2 deaths). France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. WHO estimates true DRC case count could be up to 4x higher than reported given ongoing active transmission and community mistrust limiting detection.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed cases roughly thirteenfold since early June: 400 (June 5) → 2,011 (July 15) → 3,605 (July 30) → 4,053 (August 5) → 4,665 (August 13) → 4,945 (August 16) → 5,021 (August 18) → 5,208 (August 19) → 5,290 (August 20). This is now the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide, behind only the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases). UN Senior Ebola Coordinator Julien Harneis said the outbreak is spreading 'exponentially' and that half of all deaths have occurred in just the last 20 days.

label: Deaths (2026 Outbreak)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / WHO / UN News / Al Jazeera — 20–21 August 2026
contestNote: Confirmed deaths: 2,516 DRC + 2 Uganda = 2,518 total as of 19 August, published 20 August. CFR (confirmed): ~47.6% (2,516/5,290 DRC), reaching roughly 70% in North Kivu province specifically. The toll surpassed the 2,299 deaths of DRC's 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak, making this the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history. Death toll passed 2,500 around 21 August; UN said half of all deaths have occurred in just the last 20 days. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher said the outbreak was killing one person every 30 minutes as of 14 August. WHO reports most deaths continue to occur in communities away from treatment centers.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed deaths: 64 (June 5) → 754 (July 15) → 1,587 (July 30) → 1,850 (August 5) → 2,184 (August 13) → 2,325 (August 16) → 2,378 (August 18) → 2,476 (August 19) → 2,516 (August 20). 160 confirmed cases among healthcare workers, 43-45 deaths (~27-29% CFR among HCWs). Over 260 attacks on health workers recorded across six months, eight killed.

label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
value: ~47.6% (DRC, crude, as of 19 Aug); ~70% in North Kivu
source: DRC Ministry of Health / WHO / Al Jazeera — 20–21 August 2026
contestNote: Crude national CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; DRC's overall CFR has climbed from roughly 20% in early June to ~47.6% by 19-20 August as the outbreak has spread into less-accessible, less-resourced health zones. Province-level variation is stark: North Kivu's CFR has reached roughly 70%, well above the national average, which responders and outside experts attribute to weaker treatment access rather than a change in virus behavior. BDBV historically 25–47% CFR; this outbreak's crude national CFR now sits at or above the top of the historical range.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — 70,000 Ervebo Doses Allocated, Phase 3 Trial Targeting Mid-September
value: 70,000 Ervebo doses released to DRC (20,000 for Phase 3 trial + 50,000 for frontline/health workers); human trial could begin by mid-September
source: WHO / Africa CDC / ICG / STAT News / Healio — 12–21 August 2026
contestNote: 20 August: WHO and Africa CDC announced the ICG approved immediate release of 70,000 Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) doses to DRC — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial testing cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus, 50,000 for frontline and health workers. WHO cautioned 'it is not known whether Ervebo may be protective against the Bundibugyo virus in humans,' though early lab/animal data suggest possible partial protection. As of 21 August the human trial had not yet launched; WHO/DRC talks target a start by mid-September pending shipment, DRC regulatory/ethics approval and team training. Animal data: 3/4 vaccinated primates survived BDBV challenge vs 1/4 controls; a ferret study showed 100% protection with a research-grade formulation vs 0% in controls. Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV (UK trial since 24 July) and Moderna's mRNA candidate (Canada Phase 1, early August) remain in earlier-stage animal/human safety trials and may be added later.
delta: 70,000-dose allocation approved 20 August; mid-September target date for Phase 3 launch reported 21 August
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation, 12 August trial talks, 20 August dose allocation, and a mid-September target launch are successive steps toward a structured clinical trial pathway rather than a resumption of off-label ring vaccination. Since the ICG mechanism's 2021 establishment, over 56,000 Ervebo doses have been allocated for DRC outbreaks combined, plus 167,000 doses in preventive campaigns across five countries.

label: DRC Provinces + Countries Affected
value: 6 DRC provinces (~54–55 health zones) + Uganda (outbreak closed) + France (recovered) + Germany (treated)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / WHO / UN News — 20–21 August 2026
delta: ~54-55 of 151 health zones affected as of 19-20 August, essentially unchanged since 16 August
deltaNote: Ituri Province remains the epicenter with the large majority of DRC cases (28/36 health zones, 56 new cases on 20 August alone); North Kivu (18 new cases), Haut-Uélé (7 new cases), Tshopo, South Kivu and Bas-Uélé round out the six affected provinces. UN News described the affected area as larger than France. Bas-Uélé borders Central African Republic conflict-displacement corridors and has poor road/communications access. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over 28 July. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams. The second WHO IHR Emergency Committee meeting on PHEIC status was held 18 August; Tedros said the epidemic 'is far from being under control.'

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
value: ~82.9% of identified contacts under active follow-up
delta: Coverage slipped to ~82.9% (20 August) from ~85.3% (16 August) as caseload growth outpaces tracing capacity
deltaNote: WHO/ECDC reported active follow-up at 82.9% of identified contacts as of the 20 August update, down from 85.3% on 16 August and 82.7% on 10 August — still below the 90%+ threshold needed for rapid suppression, and the outbreak's fastest-ever case growth is straining tracing teams. Mercy Corps separately warned 60-70% of new cases are recorded outside monitored contacts, with confirmed cases now just 35km from the South Sudan border; a Lancet Infectious Diseases modelling study put the probability of Ebola spillover into South Sudan at roughly 69-70%. Uganda's contact-tracing program is closed following the 28 July outbreak-end declaration. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone.
